extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies, regulatory analysts, OMB staff, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting or evaluating regulatory analyses and public comments in the context of Executive Order 14094's changes to regulatory review, with emphasis on equity, distributional impacts, public engagement, and use of a lower discount rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action threshold and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive order doubled the cost threshold for 'significant regulatory action' from $100 million to $200 million per year of impact and omitted prior language about 'novel legal or policy issues arising out of legal mandates.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret which rules qualify for centralized review under the new $200M-per-year threshold; note the narrowed scope where centralized review applies only to 'legal or policy issues for which centralized review would meaningfully further the President's priorities.' Consider whether a rule's impacts exceed the new monetary threshold and whether it implicates Presidential priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of distributive impacts and equity in regulatory analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB was directed to revise Circular A-4 to ensure that regulatory analysis recognizes 'distributive impacts and equity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory analyses should go beyond aggregate net benefits to identify who gains and who loses, quantify distributional effects where possible, and explicitly incorporate equity considerations into the analytical framework. Agencies should prepare to follow an updated Circular A-4 that operationalizes these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a lower discount rate (1.7%) for benefit-cost analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal replaced traditional discount rates of 3 percent and 7 percent with a discount rate of 1.7 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should model outcomes using the lower 1.7% discount rate (or otherwise acknowledge its effect), which increases the present value of long-term and intergenerational benefits. Commenters and agencies should show sensitivity analyses and explain how lower discounting changes benefit–cost conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement: facilitate meeting requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The order required OMB to reform the process for meetings with OIRA on proposed rules, including facilitating meeting requests to ensure access for those who have not historically participated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and OMB should adopt procedures that lower barriers to requesting meetings (e.g., clearer request processes, outreach to underrepresented stakeholders). Evaluations of engagement should consider whether historically excluded groups were enabled to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement: transparency about meeting participants
rubrics_metrics.description: The order required increasing transparency about which groups are granted meetings with OIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish lists/summaries of meetings and participants so the public can assess whose views were given privileged access. Commenters can use transparency data to argue for broader participation or to challenge unequal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity considerations as legitimate analytical factors
rubrics_metrics.description: EO 14094 emphasized that equity considerations are legitimate analytical factors in regulatory review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat equity not as an afterthought but as a central component of analysis. Describe relevant equity metrics, explain normative choices, and integrate equity discussion into the regulatory rationale and benefits assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underserved community participation as an explicit goal
rubrics_metrics.description: The order made underserved community participation an explicit goal of the regulatory process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design outreach and engagement strategies to solicit input from underserved communities; explain how the rule affects these communities and how their perspectives were solicited and considered. Use concrete plans or evidence of engagement to strengthen the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value distributional impacts (not just net benefits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distributional impacts are to be valued, not only aggregate net benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing analyses or comments, present impacts broken down by identifiable groups (e.g., income, race/ethnicity, geography) and discuss trade-offs between total efficiency and distributional equity. Provide data or reasoned argumentation about how impacts are distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments should address distributional impacts on identifiable groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments under EO 14094-era rules should address distributional impacts on identifiable groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting comments, explicitly identify which groups are affected, provide evidence or estimates of disparate impacts, and discuss whether mitigation or alternative designs could reduce inequities. Use subgroup analysis and cite relevant sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments should highlight effects on underserved communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should highlight effects on underserved communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the proposed rule would affect underserved communities specifically, provide testimony or empirical evidence where possible, and recommend modifications or targeted measures to protect or benefit these communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments should engage with non-quantified equity benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should engage with non-quantified equity benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If certain equity benefits cannot be monetized, explain their nature, importance, and how they should be weighed alongside quantified benefits. Provide qualitative evidence, case studies, or frameworks for incorporating non-quantified outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments should acknowledge the lower discount rate's effect on future-oriented analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should acknowledge the lower discount rate's effect on future-oriented analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how using a 1.7% discount rate changes the valuation of long-term or intergenerational benefits and whether that strengthens or weakens the regulatory case. Include sensitivity analyses and discuss implications for policy choices affecting future generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural expectation: OMB to revise Circular A-4 within one year
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB was directed to revise Circular A-4 within one year to reflect the order's analytical priorities (e.g., distributive impacts and equity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and commenters should anticipate and prepare for an updated Circular A-4, aligning current analyses with likely new guidance (e.g., greater emphasis on distributional metrics and different discounting). Cite the pending revision when urging particular analytical approaches.
